title: DEPACE-seq enables high-fidelity, single-nucleotide-resolution mapping of abasic sites and characterization of dynamic and long-lived AP landscapes in mammalian genomes

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and listed the only deposited archive (Zenodo 21493391, 52,669 bytes): it holds 34 files, all shell and Python analysis scripts (157,780 bytes total), and zero data files. Listed the GitHub repo it mirrors (LICENSE, README, 4 script folders, no data). Read the journal's full-text XML supplementary-material block: a single 6.45 MB PDF (gkag784_supplemental_file.pdf) is the entire supplement, with no spreadsheet or table file. Searched the full text for any sequencing accession (GEO GSE, SRA SRP/SRR, BioProject PRJ, ArrayExpress, China NGDC OMIX/CRA/HRA) and found none. Queried NCBI GEO DataSets for 'DEPACE-seq'/'DEPACE': phrase not found.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the experiments produced genome-wide AP (abasic, i.e. base-free) site maps at single-nucleotide resolution in several mammalian cell types and damage conditions, and the claimed split into long-lived versus repair-intermediate AP sites. No counts of AP sites were verifiable because no coordinate file exists. The supplementary table contents (S1 oligonucleotide sequences, S2 enzyme buffer composition, S3 HPLC conditions, S4 mass-spectrometry/NMR data) were read from in-text citations, not from the PDF itself.

a1_downloadable.note: The measured data is not downloadable anywhere. The data availability statement says only 'available within the paper and its Supplementary Information'; the Zenodo DOI holds analysis code alone (verified by download), the supplement is one PDF of chemistry methods, and no GEO, SRA, BioProject or NGDC accession appears in the text or in a GEO search. There is no file of AP-site genomic coordinates to open.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed beyond A1: with no released coordinate table there is no column of any kind. Any AP-site label would have to be regenerated from raw reads that were never deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed beyond A1. Inputs (genomic sequence windows) would come from a reference genome, but there are no site positions to attach them to.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed — stopped at the A1 failure.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessed — stopped at the A1 failure. No row count could be verified because no data file exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed — stopped at the A1 failure.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessed — stopped at the A1 failure. Nothing exists to compare against the paper's claims.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed — stopped at the A1 failure. The label would be an enzymatic-cleavage sequencing signal, which is fine in principle, but it was never released.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper released analysis scripts but not a single genomic coordinate of the abasic sites it reports, so nothing can be modelled or even counted.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence and chromatin context to predict where base-free damage sites appear in mammalian genomes.
plain_idea.train_on: The intended training set was each single-nucleotide abasic site (a position where a DNA base has been lost, leaving a gap in the code) called by DEPACE-seq, paired with its surrounding reference-genome sequence. Number of examples: unknown — no coordinate file was released.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given genomic position carries an abasic site, and whether it is a long-lived site or a short-lived repair intermediate. The true answer would come from DEPACE-seq, a chemical-labelling plus endonuclease-IV-cleavage sequencing assay.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: DNA-repair and ageing labs would get a cheap way to nominate damage hotspots without running the assay in every cell type; even a failed model would show how much abasic-site placement is sequence-encoded versus chromatin-driven.

ml_idea: Considered: train a DNA language model head (for example DNABERT-2 or HyenaDNA, both open-weight) on sequence windows around DEPACE-seq abasic-site calls to predict abasic-site propensity, with a second head separating long-lived from transient repair-intermediate sites, and a cross-cell-type transfer test. Dead on arrival because the site calls were never deposited.

effort.compute_note: No estimates made: there is no data to size. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a sequencing accession or a BED/bedGraph file of abasic-site coordinates. Done in about ten minutes: the Zenodo DOI is code only, the supplement is a PDF, and GEO has no record for DEPACE-seq.

verdict_reason: A1 failure verified in the files: the deposited archive contains only analysis scripts, and no abasic-site coordinate data was deposited anywhere.
